decision: asked the product owner 12 open behaviour questions in one batch
why: brief leaves comparisons, number formatting, arity errors, bad names, argument validation and range clamping open
result: all 12 answered and pinned in tests/test_decisions.py

decision: store cells as (row,col) -> raw + compiled formula, with a dict reverse index for single refs and a tiled RangeIndex for ranges
why: edits of unrelated cells must stay fast on a 50k-cell sheet; ranges need a lookup that is not a full scan

decision: recalculate with an iterative Tarjan SCC pass over dependents reachable from the edit
why: gives evaluation order, cycle membership (#CYCLE! only for members) and no recursion on long chains in one pass

decision: tokenizer never fails and rewriting splices only changed reference tokens
why: brief requires bytes outside rewritten references to be preserved, including in formulas that do not parse

decision: structural edits rebuild and fully recalculate the sheet
why: simplest correct design; about 1-1.4s on 50k cells measured, judged acceptable
result: open: incremental structural edits not done

decision: had a separate agent write a black-box suite from BRIEF.md only
why: review separation: catches my misreadings of the brief
result: 298/299 passed first run; the 1 failure was a wrong expectation in the test (C1=A1+1 is 11 not 12), fixed in the test

decision: ran planted-defect checks against the suite
why: confirm tests detect real defects, not just pass
result: 8 of 9 defects caught; the 9th (_MAX_TILES=0) only changes speed

decision: cached tokens on the compiled formula so rewrite does not tokenize twice
why: profile of insert_rows showed tokenize as the top cost

decision: adversarial review by a different model (fable)
result: 1 crash, 1 depth risk, 1 perf constant found

decision: non-ASCII digits in formulas tokenized as bad instead of crashing
why: str.isdigit accepts fullwidth digits but the number regex does not, so set() raised AttributeError
result: fixed, test fails on old code

decision: raise the recursion limit to 20000 during set/copy/structural edits and restore it after
why: nested (1+SUM( at 200 levels silently gave #PARSE! under pytest

decision: iter_rect reads _values directly instead of building (addr, cell) lists
why: reviewer measured 3-5x overhead per range cell

decision: comment pass removed 34 narrating comments; applied its renames and added Context protocol and type aliases
why: comments restated code or covered for unclear names

decision: committed the verbatim product owner Q&A and the benchmark script
why: trail reviewer could not resolve evidence that lived only in the session scratchpad

decision: note: rows above were written in one batch at the end of the run, not as each step landed
why: honest record of how the trail was made; order and content match the session

decision: kept full-sheet recalculation for structural edits after the reviewer measured about 0.64s per insert on 55k cells
why: an incremental version needs root-set reasoning for #REF!, shrunk ranges and broken cycles; brief names no structural-edit timing
